fact: The Projet Villages Intelligents told ANP that broadband internet connectivity had been extended to 266 communes, 339 health centres and 298 schools; it gives no total of communes and does not say in terms that the commune offices themselves are connected, and gives no date, so the date is the publication date.

ANP reports, on the project's information, that the state and World Bank Projet Villages Intelligents extended broadband internet connectivity to 266 communes alongside health centres and schools, as public services provision; no date is given, so the date is the publication date.

The Projet Villages Intelligents is implemented by a project management unit under a steering committee chaired by the national agency ANSI, seconded by the ministry of new information technologies and the ministry of economy and finance; stated as at publication.

The project is financed by the State of Niger and the World Bank/IDA at USD 100 million through IDA credits and grants (6688-NE / D656-NE), took effect in October 2020 for six years and is due to close on 23 October 2026; no domestic budget line for the communes' connectivity is named.

The communications minister said in an interview published 4 March 2025 that his ministry had drawn up a programme of interconnection and modernisation of the administration to connect all communes and the public administration within them, but that it awaited adoption of the national digital policy, the country having no adopted digital policy at that date; the interview gives no other date, so the date is its publication date.
